title: T07 Market, Limit and Stop Orders

lines.text: Lesson seven: market, limit and stop orders.
lines.say: Lesson seven: market, limit and stop orders.

lines.text: Three ways to tell an exchange what you want.
lines.say: Three ways to tell an exchange what you want.

lines.text: In T06 you worked out profit and loss. Now: how do you actually get into a trade?
lines.say: In T six you worked out profit and loss. Now: how do you actually get into a trade?

lines.text: You place an order: an instruction to the exchange to buy or sell, how much, and on what terms.
lines.say: You place an order: an instruction to the exchange to buy or sell, how much, and on what terms.

lines.text: There are three main types. Let's meet them one by one.
lines.say: There are three main types. Let's meet them one by one.

lines.text: Remember the order book from T04? Sellers' asks sit on top, buyers' bids below.
lines.say: Remember the order book from T four? Sellers' asks sit on top, buyers' bids below.

lines.text: The gap between the best ask and the best bid is the spread.
lines.say: The gap between the best ask and the best bid is the spread.

lines.text: When your order meets an order on the other side, a trade happens. That is called a fill.
lines.say: When your order meets an order on the other side, a trade happens. That is called a fill.

lines.text: A market order says: buy or sell right now, at the best price available.
lines.say: A market order says: buy or sell right now, at the best price available.

lines.text: Like buying at a stall at whatever price is asked today: quick, but you don't pick the price.
lines.say: Like buying at a stall at whatever price is asked today: quick, but you don't pick the price.

lines.text: Here we buy 0.01 BTC. It takes 0.004 at 60,010, then 0.006 at 60,020.
lines.say: Here we buy zero point zero one B-T-C. It takes zero point zero zero four at sixty thousand ten, then zero point zero zero six at sixty thousand twenty.

lines.text: Average price: 60,016 USDT. Fast, but the price was not fixed.
lines.say: Average price: sixty thousand sixteen U-S-D-T. Fast, but the price was not fixed.

lines.text: Slippage is the difference between the price you expected and the price you actually got.
lines.say: Slippage is the difference between the price you expected and the price you actually got.

lines.text: You saw a best ask of 60,010. But news hits, and the sellers move up in a flash.
lines.say: You saw a best ask of sixty thousand ten. But news hits, and the sellers move up in a flash.

lines.text: Your market order fills at 60,100. That is 90 USDT per BTC worse than expected.
lines.say: Your market order fills at sixty thousand one hundred. That is ninety U-S-D-T per B-T-C worse than expected.

lines.text: On 0.01 BTC, you paid 0.90 USDT more.
lines.say: On zero point zero one B-T-C, you paid zero point nine U-S-D-T more.

lines.text: A limit order says: buy or sell only at my price, or a better one.
lines.say: A limit order says: buy or sell only at my price, or a better one.

lines.text: Like telling a shopkeeper: call me if the price drops to my number.
lines.say: Like telling a shopkeeper: call me if the price drops to my number.

lines.text: We place a limit buy for 0.01 BTC at 59,950. It waits in the book.
lines.say: We place a limit buy for zero point zero one B-T-C at fifty-nine thousand nine hundred fifty. It waits in the book.

lines.text: Price comes down, a seller meets our price, and it fills: 599.50 USDT, no more.
lines.say: Price comes down, a seller meets our price, and it fills: five hundred ninety-nine point five U-S-D-T, no more.

lines.text: But a limit order is not guaranteed to fill.
lines.say: But a limit order is not guaranteed to fill.

lines.text: Here our limit buy at 59,900 waits. Price dips to 59,920, then rises away.
lines.say: Here our limit buy at fifty-nine thousand nine hundred waits. Price dips to fifty-nine thousand nine hundred twenty, then rises away.

lines.text: Our price was never reached, so nothing was bought. The order is still waiting.
lines.say: Our price was never reached, so nothing was bought. The order is still waiting.

lines.text: Sometimes only part of an order fills. That is a partial fill.
lines.say: Sometimes only part of an order fills. That is a partial fill.

lines.text: We want 0.01 BTC at 59,950, but only 0.004 is sold at that price.
lines.say: We want zero point zero one B-T-C at fifty-nine thousand nine hundred fifty, but only zero point zero zero four is sold at that price.

lines.text: 0.004 filled, 0.006 still waiting. You hold less than you planned.
lines.say: Zero point zero zero four filled, zero point zero zero six still waiting. You hold less than you planned.

lines.text: A stop order waits for a trigger price. Until then, nothing happens.
lines.say: A stop order waits for a trigger price. Until then, nothing happens.

lines.text: When the market reaches the trigger, the stop sends an order, often a market order.
lines.say: When the market reaches the trigger, the stop sends an order, often a market order.

lines.text: Think of a tripwire: nothing happens until price touches it, then the order goes out.
lines.say: Think of a tripwire: nothing happens until price touches it, then the order goes out.

lines.text: We hold 0.01 BTC with a stop at 59,500. Price falls, touches it, and it sells at 59,480.
lines.say: We hold zero point zero one B-T-C with a stop at fifty-nine thousand five hundred. Price falls, touches it, and it sells at fifty-nine thousand four hundred eighty.

lines.text: In a fast fall, price can jump straight past your trigger.
lines.say: In a fast fall, price can jump straight past your trigger.

lines.text: Trigger 59,500. The next trade is at 59,200. Your stop fills near 59,200.
lines.say: Trigger fifty-nine thousand five hundred. The next trade is at fifty-nine thousand two hundred. Your stop fills near fifty-nine thousand two hundred.

lines.text: That is 300 USDT per BTC of slippage, or 3 USDT on 0.01 BTC.
lines.say: That is three hundred U-S-D-T per B-T-C of slippage, or three U-S-D-T on zero point zero one B-T-C.

lines.text: A stop is a trigger, not a promise of price.
lines.say: A stop is a trigger, not a promise of price.

lines.text: Let's compare. A market order is fast, but the price is not fixed.
lines.say: Let's compare. A market order is fast, but the price is not fixed.

lines.text: A limit order controls the price, but it may fill late, in part, or never.
lines.say: A limit order controls the price, but it may fill late, in part, or never.

lines.text: A stop waits for its trigger. Once triggered, the price can still slip.
lines.say: A stop waits for its trigger. Once triggered, the price can still slip.

lines.text: A common mistake: thinking a stop order guarantees your exit price.
lines.say: A common mistake: thinking a stop order guarantees your exit price.

lines.text: It doesn't. It guarantees a trigger, and in a fast market the fill can be much worse.
lines.say: It doesn't. It guarantees a trigger, and in a fast market the fill can be much worse.

lines.text: Plan for slippage, and never treat a stop as perfect protection.
lines.say: Plan for slippage, and never treat a stop as perfect protection.

lines.text: Your turn. BTC is at 60,000. You want to buy only if it drops to 59,500, and you can wait.
lines.say: Your turn. B-T-C is at sixty thousand. You want to buy only if it drops to fifty-nine thousand five hundred, and you can wait.

lines.text: Which order type fits? Market, limit, or stop? Think it over.
lines.say: Which order type fits? Market, limit, or stop? Think it over.

lines.text: A limit buy at 59,500. The trade-off: price may never get there, and that's okay.
lines.say: A limit buy at fifty-nine thousand five hundred. The trade-off: price may never get there, and that's okay.

lines.text: Waiting, with no order at all, is always a choice too.
lines.say: Waiting, with no order at all, is always a choice too.

lines.text: Before you place any order, know what can go wrong.
lines.say: Before you place any order, know what can go wrong.

lines.text: Market orders can slip, most of all when prices move fast or the book is thin.
lines.say: Market orders can slip, most of all when prices move fast or the book is thin.

lines.text: Limit orders may fill only in part, or not at all.
lines.say: Limit orders may fill only in part, or not at all.

lines.text: Stops can fill well past the trigger. And choosing not to trade is always allowed.
lines.say: Stops can fill well past the trigger. And choosing not to trade is always allowed.

lines.text: Let's recap.
lines.say: Let's recap.

lines.text: Market: fast, price not fixed. Limit: your price or better, fill not guaranteed.
lines.say: Market: fast, price not fixed. Limit: your price or better, fill not guaranteed.

lines.text: Stop: waits for a trigger, then the fill can slip.
lines.say: Stop: waits for a trigger, then the fill can slip.

lines.text: Check yourself: which order type can stay unfilled forever?
lines.say: Check yourself: which order type can stay unfilled forever?

lines.text: A limit order, if its price is never reached.
lines.say: A limit order, if its price is never reached.

lines.text: Well done! Next up, T08: stop-loss and take-profit. Plan your exit before you enter.
lines.say: Well done! Next up, T eight: stop-loss and take-profit. Plan your exit before you enter.
